items.title: 卧槽，补丁一发，AI 拿着新旧两个二进制就能反推出漏洞❗️
items.summary:
卧槽，补丁一发，AI 拿着新旧两个二进制就能反推出漏洞❗️

新加坡国立、伯克利几所学校出了个评测，叫 CyberBinGym，Dawn Song 也在作者里
做法很狠：只给 AI 一个没打补丁的 stripped 二进制、一个打了补丁的，不给源码，不给漏洞描述
让它自己对比、调试，找出洞，再打出 exploit 拿 flag

100 个任务，来自 53 个常用开源项目的真实漏洞，6 类漏洞、3 档难度
还人工审了 AI 的操作轨迹，防它走捷径刷分

结果
Codex 配 GPT-5.6，88% 找到了漏洞，真正打通 exploit 的是 20%
Claude Code 配 Opus 5，找洞 85%，打通只有 6%
Kimi Code 配 K3，找洞 64%，一个都没打通😂

同一批 20 个任务，多给它补丁版二进制，exploit 成功率从 10% 涨到 25%
开了 canary、PIE、full RELRO 这些常规加固，原来打通的 20 个里还能打穿 2 个

做逆向的看到这个应该很有感觉
以前 patch diff 是老师傅的活，开着 bindiff 一个函数一个函数对
现在 AI 找洞已经挺稳了，卡在最后写利用这一步

说人话就是，补丁发布那一刻，攻击者的倒计时也开始了
修复按周算的团队，这个窗口正在被 AI 压缩
能自动更新的赶紧开，内网那堆等维护窗口再升级的机器最危险

items.title: 当今时代男生最掉价的九大行为：
items.summary:
当今时代男生最掉价的九大行为：

1. 从来没用过 Claude 和 GPT，还觉得 DeepSeek 就是 AI 的天花板。
2. 不知道什么叫 MCP，连 Agent、Skills、Harness 的区别都搞不清楚。
3. 不会用 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor，至今还在一行行手搓代码、一页页手搓 PPT。
4. 没有自己的知识库，资料全散在微信收藏和网盘里，AI 每次都只能从零开始。
5. 还在网页上复制粘贴跟 AI 聊天，从没让 AI 直接动手改过自己电脑里的文件。
6. 一个对话聊到天荒地老，不知道 Token 怎么算钱，钱烧光了还嫌 AI 变笨了。
7. 不懂 GPU、CUDA、VRAM、显存带宽，甚至不知道为什么推理需要大量算力。
8. 没搭过 Multi-Agent 工作流，不会用 Docker、API、Webhook，更没听过 LangGraph。

最致命的是，以上八条全中，却天天在朋友圈转发AI 将取代 90% 的人。😃

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary:
In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.” [...] The sooner the better, the researchers suggest. “Moving too slowly with AI governance means you may miss out on opportunities,” Saripalli says. “The board has fiduciary responsibility for anything that has impact at the product or service level.”

“The risk of not moving is as serious as the risk of AI systems running amok,” Matthys adds, noting how past technological shifts have left unprepared companies behind. “If you don’t keep up, there’s a risk that 20 years from now you won’t exist.” [...] ## In Brief

 A new survey finds that corporate boards are not keeping up with AI governance.
 Directors report that they are discussing and using AI, yet their boards lack a systematic approach to oversight.
 Companies that wait to define AI strategy and audit their AI use risk being left behind.

“We’re trying to change the wheels on the bus while driving it at 100 miles an hour downhill.”

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary:
In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.” [...] The sooner the better, the researchers suggest. “Moving too slowly with AI governance means you may miss out on opportunities,” Saripalli says. “The board has fiduciary responsibility for anything that has impact at the product or service level.”

“The risk of not moving is as serious as the risk of AI systems running amok,” Matthys adds, noting how past technological shifts have left unprepared companies behind. “If you don’t keep up, there’s a risk that 20 years from now you won’t exist.” [...] ## In Brief

 A new survey finds that corporate boards are not keeping up with AI governance.
 Directors report that they are discussing and using AI, yet their boards lack a systematic approach to oversight.
 Companies that wait to define AI strategy and audit their AI use risk being left behind.

“We’re trying to change the wheels on the bus while driving it at 100 miles an hour downhill.”

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

These materials are promising compounds for solar cells. AutoBot studied metal halide perovskites—promising materials for light-transforming devices such as solar cells and detectors—by testing how humidity during manufacturing affects their quality. Instead of examining all 5,000 possible combinations of temperature, process timing, and humidity, the SI system selected only the most informative [...] This work could revolutionize how scientists develop new materials. Instead of scientists spending months or years testing thousands of combinations by hand, machine learning-driven robots can find the best solutions in days to a few weeks. This advance promises to lower costs while dramatically speeding up the creation of better solar panels, computer chips, and other electronics. items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.
